author: Mark Atwood
text:
Spec-line update (2026-05-11): the spec edit captured by `JMAP-kt5k` landed today as commit `80d5e11` on jmap-chat-spec. The bead description's spec line citations (lines 1095, 1108, 1117, 1126) are now stale — the per-aggregate cap enforcement language was rewritten and the dropped field names (`maxRolesPerSpace`, `maxSpaceMembers`, `maxChannelsPerSpace`, `maxCategoriesPerSpace`) are no longer mentioned in the spec.

What this changes for the implementation here: nothing structural. The bead's chosen approach — `ChatBackend::limits()` returning a `ChatLimits` struct, handler queries it and rejects over-cap requests with `overQuota` SetError — is now spec-mandated (not just workspace-preferred). The spec now reads, for each of the four Space/set add* ops:

> "If the resulting [role|member|channel|category] count would exceed a server-defined limit on the number of [...] per Space, the server MUST return an `overQuota` SetError ({{RFC8620}} §5.3)."

The `ChatLimits` baseline defaults from the bead's "Notes" section (max_roles_per_space = 50, max_space_members = 10_000, max_channels_per_space = 500, max_categories_per_space = 100) are unaffected — they're implementation defaults, not spec values.

Workspace AGENTS.md "Backend caps and limits" section already documents this pattern as canonical for the workspace.

Related: JMAP-v3ff covers the parallel catch-up work in `jmap-chat-client::ChatCapability` (which still carries the 5 dropped fields) and a stale doc comment in `crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:168–169` that cites the dropped spec field names.
